metadata.title: Reviews of National Policies for Education: Denmark 2004 (EN) — Lessons from PISA 2000

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD review synthesizes evidence from PISA 2000 and earlier international assessments rather than estimating student-level models with microdata. The text reports descriptive and comparative statistics (e.g., mean scores, between/within-school variation, achievement gaps) and discusses policy implications; it does not document the use of PISA sampling weights or replicate-weight variance estimation in an analytic model. Because no student-level regression/ML estimation is presented, there is no explicit weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to extract. For replication with PISA microdata, analysts would typically apply PISA sampling weights and plausible-value procedures, but this report itself does not specify such a workflow.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because the document is a policy review that summarizes published PISA results (means, gaps, and variation measures) and does not report an original student-level achievement modeling pipeline that would require PV generation/combination. Missing-data handling is not reported because the analysis is not presented as a re-analysis of microdata with an explicit analytic sample and imputation/deletion strategy; instead, it relies on OECD/IEA-published statistics and qualitative policy evidence. As a result, there is no methodological section describing how missing questionnaire or achievement data were treated in an estimation model.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report does not define an analytic student-level sample for an original quantitative model. It uses published PISA 2000 results for Denmark and selected reference countries (Canada—Province of Alberta, Finland, United Kingdom) and also references other international assessments (e.g., TIMSS, IEA reading literacy). Therefore, no inclusion/exclusion criteria for an extracted microdata analytic sample are provided.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD policy review uses PISA 2000 as an evidence base to assess the quality and equity of Denmark’s primary and lower secondary schooling outcomes, focusing on reading literacy (main emphasis), with lighter treatment of mathematical and scientific literacy. It reports comparative performance indicators such as Denmark’s mean reading score (497, close to OECD 500), mathematics (514), and science (481), alongside equity-related statistics including achievement gaps by gender, home background, and immigrant status, and between- vs within-school variation. The report also draws on qualitative evidence from site visits (eight schools) and interviews, and it explicitly notes that PISA data cannot establish causality. No student-level predictive modeling or ML pipeline is estimated in the document; instead, it synthesizes published PISA results and uses them to motivate policy recommendations (e.g., strengthening evaluation culture, early reading support, and teacher training). Limitations include reliance on cross-sectional test snapshots and the absence of a documented re-analysis workflow with PV and missing-data procedures.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse for ML-specific fields because the document is an OECD policy review that does not present an original empirical ML estimation with a defined analytic sample, target variables, model training, or reported predictive metrics. The quantitative content is descriptive/comparative (published PISA statistics) and the qualitative content is based on expert visits and document analysis. Consequently, fields such as total_students, PV handling for an estimation model, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not applicable or not reported in the sense required for an empirical ML paper.
